rounds.text: Vikram Solar Ltd carries severe structural and momentum risks despite backward-looking fundamental growth. The technical and institutional setup is heavily compromised: the stock sits a mere 9% of the way up its 52-year range at ₹183, trading well below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a wretched relative-strength rating of 9 against the Nifty 500 [E5, E43, E44]. Institutional sentiment mirrors this price destruction, showing negative money flow as domestic institutions slashed holdings from 6.20% to 4.04% alongside a broader multi-year promoter stake reduction of 30.1% [E36, E37, E55]. Operational consistency is also fraying beneath the headline figures, highlighted by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend and a recent quarterly margin contraction of two percentage points year-over-year [E24, E25, E26]. Furthermore, borrowings more than doubled to ₹617 Cr in Mar 2026 from ₹272 Cr a year prior, while the company yields 0.00% and refuses to pay dividends despite reporting profits [E4, E32, E54]. Conceded: the company displays robust trailing financial metrics, including a 240% TTM profit growth, a strong ROCE of 30.6%, and an operating cash flow of ₹667 Cr that fully backs reported earnings [E19, E12, E27, E28].
